sections.label: The brief
sections.html: Every retailer runs returns differently, with its own windows, fees, and outcomes. ReturnLogic’s portal had to fit each retailer’s policy instead of making the retailer bend to the software.

sections.label: A return, start to finish
sections.html:
1. StartShopper portalWhere a shopper starts a return. Each retailer could customize all of it: design, text, flow, and step order.
  2. PriceReturn calculationsWhat the shopper gets back after fees, accounting for discounts and promos, tax and shipping, and the price difference on exchanges. Bundles come back whole or item by item, as the retailer chooses.
  3. ApproveAuto authorizationA return that meets the retailer’s rules is approved and gets its shipping label, through EasyPost or the retailer’s own carrier account.
  4. CloseAutomated processingThe refund, gift card, or exchange item goes out and the return is closed, with no one touching it.

I built every step. Teammates built the return rules engine and return analytics; I contributed to analytics.

sections.label: The hard part
sections.html:
Everything in the portal was configurable per retailer, and the settings interacted, so there were far more combinations than anyone could test by hand.

I kept it manageable three ways: defaults plus overrides, so a retailer only set what differed; LaunchDarkly flags to roll changes out retailer by retailer; and Jest tests on the risky combinations.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.html:
In 2026 a major reverse-logistics competitor acquired ReturnLogic.

  • 2M+Returns processed
